topic: Journey into the Infinite: The Riemann Zeta Function
target_audience: University STEM students and advanced high school mathematics enthusiasts

sections.title: The Infinite Staircase: Prerequisite Knowledge
lecture_lines: Infinite sums don't always reach infinity.
Zeno’s rabbit jumps halfway, then half again.
He approaches the wall but never crosses.
animations: Draw a white horizontal line (#FFFFFF) from x=-4 to x=4, labeled '0' at x=-4 and '1' at x=4.
A green circle (#00FF00) 'Zeno' jumps from '0' to the center (1/2). Label '1/2' appears below the jump.
Zeno jumps to 3/4 and then 7/8. Labels '1/4' and '1/8' appear. A red arrow (#FF0000) highlights the remaining distance to '1'.

sections.title: Defining the Zeta Function: The Summation Rule
lecture_lines: The Zeta function defines an infinite power sum.
Variable s determines how fast terms shrink.
Inputting s equals two yields pi squared over six.
At s equals one, the series overflows to infinity.
This boundary defines where the sum converges.
animations: Display formula 'zeta(s) = sum(1/n^s)' in yellow (#FFFF00) at top-center.
The sum expands into '1/1^s + 1/2^s + 1/3^s +...' in white (#FFFFFF) below the formula.
A cyan rectangle (#00FFFF) 'Number Factory' appears. An arrow labeled 's=2' enters the factory.
The factory flashes; 'pi^2/6' emerges. A new equation 'sum(1/n^2) = pi^2/6' appears in gold (#FFD700).
Input 's=1' enters the factory. Factory turns red (#FF4500), displaying 'Divergent' as the terms fail to shrink fast enough.

sections.title: The Prime Connection: The Euler Product Formula
lecture_lines: Euler linked the Zeta function to prime numbers.
The sum transforms into an infinite product of primes.
Zeta acts as a DNA map for all primes.
animations: The sum 'sum(1/n^s)' on left and the product 'product(1/(1-p^-s))' on right appear in white (#FFFFFF).
Three spinning lime green gears (#7FFF00) labeled '2, 3, 5' appear between the sum and product, interlocking.
Gears transform into a golden bridge (#FFD700) with text 'Primes = DNA' appearing above the connection.

sections.title: Analytic Continuation: Crossing the Barrier
lecture_lines: We can extend Zeta beyond its original limits.
Analytic continuation stretches the function across complex space.
This reveals hidden values in the negative plane.
It leads to the counter-intuitive sum of natural numbers.
The 'impossible' result equals negative one twelfth.
animations: A blue-shaded region (#4682B4) for Re(s) > 1 appears on a grid. Formula 'zeta(s) = sum(n^-s)' sits inside it.
A purple mesh grid (#BA55D3) stretches out from the blue region to cover the entire screen.
A red circle with a cross (#FF0000) marks the pole at s=1 (the only point not covered).
A white magnifying circle highlights s = -1. Formula 'zeta(-1) = -1/12' appears in bright green (#00FF00) nearby.
The 'stretching' mesh pulses to emphasize the 'Analytic Continuation' process.

sections.title: The Million Dollar Mystery: The Riemann Hypothesis
lecture_lines: Zeros are points where the function equals zero.
Non-trivial zeros seem to align on one line.
This critical line sits at real part one half.
The Riemann Hypothesis predicts they all lie here.
Proving this unlocks the secrets of prime numbers.
animations: Draw a bright blue vertical line (#1E90FF) at Re(s) = 1/2 labeled 'Critical Line'.
A semi-transparent dark grey rectangle (#2F4F4F) shades the 'Critical Strip' from Re(s)=0 to Re(s)=1.
Yellow dots (#FFFF00) 'Zeros' pop up one by one along the blue Critical Line.
An orange dot (#FF8C00) tries to appear off-line but is cancelled by a red 'X'.
A golden treasure chest icon (#FFD700) with label '$1,000,000' appears at the bottom.

sections.title: Application: The Rhythm of Physics
lecture_lines: Zeta isn't just abstract; it's in our universe.
It tames infinite energy in the Casimir effect.
This bridge links pure math to physical reality.
animations: Two silver vertical rectangles (#C0C0C0) 'Metal Plates' appear center-screen.
Blue wavy lines (#00BFFF) representing quantum fluctuations oscillate between the plates.
Plates move closer. Calculation 'zeta(-3)' appears in light green (#ADFF2F) to show the force prediction.
